L: B
[Have you ever tried] ice fishing?
너는 얼음낚시를 해 본 적이 있니?
G
[Yes, I have], Alex. I went to an ice festival last winter and tried ice fishing there.
응, 있어, Alex. 나는 지난겨울에 얼음 축제에 가서 거기서 얼음낚시를 해 봤어.
B
That's great! My family [is planning to] go ice fishing this winter.
멋지다! 우리 가족은 이번 겨울에 얼음낚시를 하러 갈 계획이야.
G
Oh, you're going to love it. It's really exciting.
오, 너는 그걸 정말 좋아할 거야. 정말 신나.
B
Yeah. [I'm looking forward to] fishing on the icy river.
응. 나는 얼어붙은 강에서 낚시하는 것이 기대돼.
B
Reena, do you [have any plans] this weekend?
Reena, 이번 주말에 무슨 계획이 있니?
G
Yes, I'm [going camping] with my family.
응, 나는 가족과 캠핑을 갈 거야.
B
That sounds fun! [Have you ever roasted] marshmallows [while] camping?
재미있겠다! 너는 캠핑하면서 마시멜로를 구워 본 적이 있니?
G
[No, I haven't], but I want to try.
아니, 없어, 하지만 해 보고 싶어.
B
When you roast marshmallows, they [become] so soft and sweet.
마시멜로를 구우면, 아주 부드럽고 달콤해져.
G
Oh, that sounds delicious. [I'm really looking forward to] tasting them.
오, 맛있겠다. 나는 그것들을 맛보는 것이 정말 기대돼.
B
[Have you ever been to] Boryeong?
너는 보령에 가 본 적이 있니?
G
[Yes, I have], James. I went there last summer for the mud festival.
응, 있어, James. 나는 지난여름에 머드 축제 때문에 거기에 갔어.
B
Oh, really? I'm going to the next mud festival. What activities did you enjoy?
오, 정말? 나는 다음 머드 축제에 갈 거야. 너는 어떤 활동들을 즐겼니?
G
I [rode] the mud slide and played in the mud pool.
나는 머드 미끄럼틀을 탔고 머드 풀에서 놀았어.
B
Sounds exciting! [I'm looking forward to] [trying out] all the muddy activities.
신나겠다! 나는 진흙투성이 활동들을 모두 해 보는 것이 기대돼.
G
Yeah, [I hope] you have a fantastic time!
그래, 네가 환상적인 시간을 보내길 바라!
G
These strawberries are really delicious. [Have you ever picked] fresh strawberries, Giho?
이 딸기들은 정말 맛있어. 너는 신선한 딸기를 따 본 적이 있니, 기호야?
B
[Yes, I have]. I picked these strawberries [myself].
응, 있어. 내가 이 딸기들을 직접 땄어.
G
Really? Where did you pick them?
정말? 그것들을 어디에서 땄니?
B
I [participated in] a strawberry picking event at a farm last week.
나는 지난주에 농장에서 열린 딸기 따기 행사에 참가했어.
G
That sounds really interesting. [Can you tell me more about] the event?
정말 흥미롭다. 그 행사에 대해 좀 더 말해 줄 수 있니?
B
Of course. You can eat all the strawberries you pick at the farm.
물론이지. 농장에서 네가 딴 딸기는 모두 먹을 수 있어.
G
[How many] strawberries did you eat?
너는 딸기를 몇 개나 먹었니?
B
I don't know [exactly], but I was [so full].
정확히는 모르겠지만, 나는 정말 배가 불렀어.
G
[Sounds like] you had a great time. Are you going to go there again?
즐거운 시간을 보낸 것 같네. 거기에 다시 갈 거니?
B
Yes. Next month. [I'm looking forward to] picking those fresh strawberries again.
응. 다음 달에. 나는 그 신선한 딸기들을 다시 따는 것이 기대돼.
Lucy
My friend Emily is visiting Seoul this weekend. Where can I [take] her?
내 친구 Emily가 이번 주말에 서울을 방문해. 내가 그녀를 어디로 데려갈 수 있을까?
Giho
Well, Lucy, [have you ever visited] Hanyangdoseong before?
음, Lucy, 전에 한양도성을 방문해 본 적이 있니?
Lucy
[No, I haven't]. What's that?
아니, 없어. 그게 뭐야?
Giho
It's an [ancient] wall [surrounding] Seoul.
그건 서울을 둘러싸고 있는 오래된 성벽이야.
Lucy
That sounds interesting. What can we do there?
흥미롭다. 우리는 거기서 무엇을 할 수 있어?
Giho
You can [walk along] the wall and enjoy the beautiful view. You can also [participate in] a stamp tour.
성벽을 따라 걸으면서 아름다운 경치를 즐길 수 있어. 스탬프 투어에도 참가할 수 있어.
Lucy
That's perfect. Emily likes walking. And she'll love the stamp tour.
완벽해. Emily는 걷는 것을 좋아해. 그리고 그녀는 스탬프 투어를 아주 좋아할 거야.
Giho
[I hope] you have a great time at Hanyangdoseong.
네가 한양도성에서 즐거운 시간을 보내길 바라.
Lucy
Thanks. [I'm really looking forward to] walking around the city with Emily.
고마워. 나는 Emily와 도시를 걸어 다니는 것이 정말 기대돼.
A
Nara, [have you taken] a dance class before?
나라야, 전에 춤 수업을 들어 본 적이 있니?
B
[No, I haven't]. Why do you ask?
아니, 없어. 왜 물어보니?
A
I'm going to take a dance class this weekend. [Would you like to] join me?
나는 이번 주말에 춤 수업을 들을 거야. 나와 함께 할래?
B
Of course. [I'd love to]!
물론이지. 꼭 하고 싶어!
A
Great. [I'm looking forward to] it.
좋아. 나는 그것이 기대돼.
B
Minha, [have you ever been to] the Jeonju Bibimbap Festival?
민하야, 너는 전주 비빔밥 축제에 가 본 적이 있니?
G
[Yes, I have]. I went there last year.
응, 있어. 나는 작년에 거기에 갔어.
B
Oh, really? I'm going to the festival this year. What did you do there?
오, 정말? 나는 올해 그 축제에 갈 거야. 너는 거기서 무엇을 했니?
G
I [participated in] a bibimbap-making contest.
나는 비빔밥 만들기 대회에 참가했어.
B
Sounds exciting! [I'm looking forward to] tasting different kinds of bibimbap.
신나겠다! 나는 여러 가지 종류의 비빔밥을 맛보는 것이 기대돼.
G
Great. [I hope] you have a great time!
좋아. 네가 즐거운 시간을 보내길 바라!
G
Junho, do you [have any plans] this weekend?
준호야, 이번 주말에 무슨 계획이 있니?
B
Yes. I'm [planning to] go to an ice fishing festival with my family.
응. 나는 가족과 얼음낚시 축제에 갈 계획이야.
G
That sounds fun! [Have you ever gone to] an ice fishing festival before?
재미있겠다! 전에 얼음낚시 축제에 가 본 적이 있니?
B
[No, I haven't].
아니, 없어.
G
You'll love it! [Catching] fish from an ice hole is a lot of fun.
너는 그걸 정말 좋아할 거야! 얼음 구멍에서 물고기를 잡는 것은 정말 재미있어.
B
Oh, that sounds amazing. [I'm looking forward to] catching many fish.
오, 굉장하다. 나는 물고기를 많이 잡는 것이 기대돼.

body.sub: The Quebec Winter Carnival · Did You Know?
lines: Hello! Welcome to the Quebec Winter Carnival.
I am Bonhomme, the mascot of the carnival. I am a big snowman.
As you can see, I’m wearing a big red hat and a special belt.
Do you want to take home an unforgettable memory from the carnival?
Follow me, and I’ll show you what to do here.
Bonhomme means “good man” in French.
The Quebec Winter Carnival is usually held for 10 days between January and February in Quebec, Canada.
This is my ice palace.
Every year, a new ice palace is built for the carnival.
So, I have a new home each year!
Because the palace is made of ice and snow, it shines beautifully during the day.
At night, it is even more beautiful with many lights.
Take a look at my fantastic ice garden.
You can see amazing ice sculptures of trees, flowers, and animals here.
You can also enjoy exciting concerts and performances.
Do you like to dance? I can teach you how to dance like me.
There are also so many interesting activities you can do at the carnival.
The toboggan slide was built in 1884 and is 200 meters long.
A toboggan is a long narrow sled.
If you like speed, get on the toboggan.
It is so fast that you will feel like you are on a roller coaster.
While you’re sliding down, you can enjoy amazing views of Quebec.
You can see a huge famous castle on your left.
On your right, you can see a beautiful icy river.
If you see a large crowd along the river, it’s time to watch the Ice Canoe Race.
This race is one of the best parts of the carnival, and you shouldn’t miss it.
Canoe teams have to race through the icy river for about three kilometers.
Teams are usually made up of five members, and both men and women can join the team.
Look! One team is stuck in the ice and can’t move!
The members have to push their canoe on the ice to get to the water.
Phew! They are in the water again.
I hope they can make it to the finish line.
The race is so exciting that you will forget about the cold.
After all these exciting activities, I’m really hungry.
There are many delicious treats to eat at the carnival.
How about a cup of hot chocolate?
It’s always the perfect drink in cold weather.
You also have to try maple taffy.
It’s made in a special way here.
Let’s learn how to make it.
Pour hot maple syrup on the snow.
Then place a stick on the syrup and quickly roll it around.
Now, you have delicious maple taffy!
I hope you come and see me at the carnival.
Oh, don’t forget to check our website for more information. Bye!
